title: Siau Island flash floods kill at least 16
detail: Overnight rain overflowed rivers across four Siau districts; BNPB reported at least 16 dead, 3 missing, 18 injured and 682 displaced, with 7 homes swept away. A 14-day emergency was declared.

title: Anti-Scam Centre returns Rp161 billion to victims
detail: OJK said the Indonesia Anti-Scam Centre returned Rp161 billion to 1,070 victims; from Nov 22, 2024 to Jan 12, 2026 it logged 432,637 complaints with reported losses of Rp9.1 trillion and blocked Rp436.88 billion.

title: Burangrang landslide buries Pasirlangu, 82 missing
detail: A rain-triggered landslide and flash flood from Mount Burangrang struck about 30 homes in Pasirlangu village; BNPB initially reported 7 dead and 82 missing.

title: BNN busts meth and cannabis networks, 360 kg seized
detail: BNN said it dismantled a Golden Triangle-linked meth network in Aceh (160 kg, worth about Rp208 billion) and an Aceh-to-Medan cannabis route (200 kg), arresting suspects in both.

title: M6.2 megathrust quake off Pacitan injures 36
detail: BMKG recorded a M6.2 quake at 58 km depth off Pacitan at 01:06; local BPBDs reported at least 36 injured and 35 buildings damaged in Pacitan and Bantul.

title: Smart Air plane shot at Korowai airstrip, two pilots killed
detail: An armed separatist group opened fire on a Smart Air aircraft at Korowai airport, killing both pilots; all 13 passengers were rescued. The Cartenz Peace Task Force blamed two Yahukimo-based KKB battalions.
attribution: Cartenz Peace Task Force via Antara

title: BBMKG Denpasar warns of extreme weather and high waves in Bali to 17 Feb
detail: The Region III meteorology office warned all nine Bali districts of heavy rain, thunderstorms and gusty winds from 11 to 17 February, with 1.25-2.5 m waves in the southern straits and possible floods and landslides.

title: Govt speeds return of 4,254 Indonesians from Cambodia
detail: Kemlu said 4,254 Indonesians registered with the Phnom Penh embassy from Jan 16 to Feb 15 amid Cambodia's scam crackdown; staged flights ran Feb 16-Mar 4. It said many admitted scam involvement and screening of 3,917 found no trafficking victims.

title: Police probe Rp25 trillion laundering tied to illegal gold
detail: The National Police, working with PPATK, raided two houses and a jewellery shop in Surabaya and Nganjuk, seizing cash, gold and documents in a probe of about Rp25 trillion allegedly laundered from an illegal West Kalimantan gold mine (2019-2022).

title: Bantargebang landfill slide kills 5; Jakarta halts dumping in zone 4A
detail: A waste-pile landslide in zone 4A of Jakarta's Bantargebang landfill in Bekasi killed five with four missing; the Environment Minister called it a systemic failure and Governor Pramono Anung halted open dumping in the zone, which receives 7,400-8,000 tonnes a day.

title: Health Ministry: 58 measles outbreaks in 14 provinces; health workers told to be vigilant
detail: The Health Ministry reported 58 measles outbreaks across 39 districts and cities in 14 provinces by week 11, with about 2,740 early-2026 cases falling sharply; it issued a circular requiring isolation, PPE and 24-hour reporting, and ran outbreak immunisation in 102 districts.

title: BPOM approves wider adult use of domestic measles vaccine
detail: The food and drug agency approved expanded use of Bio Farma's measles vaccine for at-risk adults such as health workers and travellers from 7 April, citing persistent transmission risk after the year's outbreaks.

title: Govt weighs US request for military overflight access
detail: Foreign Minister Sugiono said Indonesia is reviewing a US letter of intent seeking overflight access for US military aircraft, weighing sovereignty; Reuters earlier reported the foreign ministry privately warned of security risks.

title: 26 foreigners, mostly Filipinos, found in Kuta scam operation
detail: Denpasar police raided a Kuta hotel and detained 26 foreigners, mainly Filipinos; the Philippine embassy said its citizens were being held by the syndicate to work as scam operators. Trafficking charges were under consideration.
attribution: Police, immigration and Philippine embassy via Antara

title: Argo Bromo Anggrek rams stationary KRL at Bekasi Timur; 16 dead
detail: The long-distance Argo Bromo Anggrek struck a stopped KRL commuter train at East Bekasi Station on the evening of 27 April, killing 16 and injuring 91; police said the commuter train had been halted by a taxi stalled on a level crossing and are probing human error and signalling faults.

title: Jakarta floods hit 115 neighbourhood units
detail: Heavy rain overflowed seven rivers including the Ciliwung, Krukut and Pesanggrahan, flooding 115 neighbourhood units (78 in South Jakarta) to depths of 15 cm to 2.4 m, Jakarta BPBD said.

title: Densus 88 arrests eight JAD suspects in Central Sulawesi
detail: Densus 88 arrested eight suspects linked to IS-affiliated Jamaah Anshoru Daulah, four in Parigi Moutong and four in Poso, alleged to have spread extremist propaganda online, a National Police spokesperson said.

title: 210 foreigners detained in Batam fake-trading scam raid
detail: Batam immigration and a joint team raided Baloi View apartments, detaining 210 foreigners (125 Vietnamese, 84 Chinese, 1 Myanmar) allegedly running fake stock/forex trading apps targeting victims in Europe and Vietnam; hundreds of devices and 198 passports seized.

title: Bareskrim arrests 321 foreigners in online gambling raid
detail: Bareskrim said it arrested 321 foreign nationals, mostly Vietnamese (228) and Chinese (57), running an online gambling operation in Jakarta linked to about 75 domains.

title: Police report 1,241 counterfeit-money suspects
detail: Bareskrim said 252 counterfeit currency cases in 2025-2026 led to 1,241 arrests and seizure of 137,005 fake rupiah and 17,267 fake US dollar notes; it destroyed 466,535 fake notes.

title: Firefight in Dekai; TPNPB claims retaliatory killing
detail: TPNPB said two of its fighters died in a clash with security forces in Dekai and claimed it shot dead one soldier in retaliation; the soldier's death was not confirmed by Indonesian authorities.
attribution: TPNPB claims via Jubi (unconfirmed by TNI/Polri)

title: Border task force trains anti-drone surveillance at Entikong
detail: The Indonesia-Malaysia Border Security Task Force ran counter-drone drills at Entikong and Temajuk, citing drone risks tied to illegal crossings, smuggling and espionage, its commander said.

title: OJK launches National Fraud Portal
detail: OJK launched a National Fraud Portal in the Anti-Scam Centre; it reported 14,232 complaints Jan-Apr 29, 2026 (11,753 on illegal online loans) and 951 illegal lending entities shut by the PASTI task force.

title: Pig-butchering ring busted in Sukoharjo, 39 suspects
detail: Central Java police named 39 suspects, including 11 from Nepal and Myanmar, in a romance-crypto fraud ring that allegedly took about Rp41.1 billion from 133 mostly US victims between Jul 2025 and May 2026.

title: Two gold refiner directors detained in illegal-gold laundering case
detail: Bareskrim detained a former and the current director of a gold company on suspicion of processing and selling gold from illegal mines and money laundering, adding to three suspects from a Nganjuk gold business; PPATK is tracing assets.

title: US pilot killed as mission aircraft shot at in Yahukimo
detail: Gunmen fired on an Associated Mission Aviation (AMA) aircraft flying Wamena to Balinggama, killing its American pilot. The Cartenz task force attributed the attack to a newly emerged 'Bakusip' faction.
attribution: Cartenz Peace Task Force via Antara

title: Repatriation requests from Cambodia hit 11,986 in H1
detail: Kemlu's citizen-protection director said 11,986 Indonesians requested repatriation from Cambodia in Jan-Jun 2026, more than double the 5,088 in all of 2025, as Cambodia raided scam compounds.

title: Rolling blackouts hit Java-Bali grid; government orders PLN fixes
detail: Rolling blackouts in mid-2026 hit millions on the Java-Bali grid, including South Tangerang and Depok; PLN blamed a shortage of suitable-grade coal. On 3 July the government ordered PLN to secure fuel supply and speed generator maintenance. Asia Times reported emergency coal shipments later ended the rolling cuts.
agency: PLN / Energy and Mineral Resources Ministry
attribution: Asia Times; government order per ANTARA (en.antaranews.com/news/421431)

title: OJK: 557,000 suspected scam accounts blocked
detail: OJK said the Anti-Scam Centre had blocked over 557,000 suspected accounts from 608,000+ scam reports as of June 2026, freezing Rp674 billion and returning about Rp200 billion.
attribution: OJK figures via Fintech News Indonesia

title: BMKG: Cyclone Bavi brings strong winds and 4 m waves to eastern Indonesia
detail: BMKG said Tropical Cyclone Bavi, north of Papua and moving west, threatened strong winds in North Sulawesi, North Maluku, Southwest Papua and West Papua, with waves of 2.5-4.0 m north of Maluku and West Papua.
place: Waters north of Papua and Maluku

title: TNI AU and RMAF fly joint border air patrol
detail: Two Indonesian F-16s and two Malaysian F/A-18s flew the Malindo coordinated patrol along the shared maritime border, the TNI AU spokesperson said.

title: 32,500 gambling-linked bank accounts closed
detail: Komdigi said 3.7 million gambling sites/content were blocked and 38,000 suspected gambling-linked accounts referred, of which 32,500 were closed (Oct 20, 2024-Jul 12, 2026); PPATK data put 2025 online-gambling transactions at Rp286.84 trillion.

title: BNN: 1,259 drug arrests in 2026 across 34 provinces
detail: BNN head Suyudi Ario Seto said 2026 operations produced 1,259 arrests, 126.3 kg of meth, a 3.37 t cannabis interception in Gresik and a mephedrone lab bust in Bali; the agency cited 12.3 t seized over 21 months.

title: M7.7 quake off Flores kills at least 47
detail: A magnitude 7.7 quake at 10 km depth struck about 68 km NNW of Ende, killing at least 47, destroying 157 houses and damaging about 200; a tsunami warning was issued then lifted and about 2,000 villagers in Nagekeo evacuated.

title: 2.6 t liquid meth seized from Tanzanian-flagged ship
detail: BNN, Customs and Riau Islands police intercepted the MV Ocean Porter in Riau waters with 2.6 tons of liquid methamphetamine, arresting 10 Myanmar crew; officials said the cargo was tied to trafficking from Sarawak.

title: Navy says 514 t of illegal minerals seized in 2026
detail: The Fleet Command said it seized 514.1 tons of illegally mined minerals (tin sand, coal) worth Rp10.25 trillion so far in 2026, incl. 75.7 t of tin sand off Bangka Belitung on Aug 2-13, and 1.3 t of drugs.

title: Govt marks fourth year without terror attack
detail: Deputy Coordinating Minister Lodewijk F. Paulus said Indonesia had entered a fourth year with zero terrorist attacks; BNPT head Eddy Hartono said 28 planned attacks were thwarted over four years.

title: About 475 Indonesians held in Phnom Penh after scam crackdown
detail: At least 475 Indonesians who had worked in Cambodian scam operations were held at a facility near Pochentong airport awaiting repatriation; detainees said embassy support ended Aug 30 for lack of funds.
attribution: Phnom Penh Post via The Star

title: Krakatau ash cancels 1,558 flights, eight airports shut
detail: Anak Krakatau eruptions sent ash to high altitude, closing eight airports including Soekarno-Hatta and Halim in Jakarta; AP reported 1,558 flights cancelled affecting about 170,000 passengers, citing aviation authorities.

title: BNPB: 1,730 disasters Jan 1-Sep 7
detail: BNPB reported 1,730 disasters from Jan 1 to Sep 7, 2026, led by wildfires (627), floods (543), extreme weather (324), landslides (105) and droughts (101), plus 13 major earthquakes and 3 volcanic eruptions; 111,533 homes damaged.

title: Ferry capsizes in Java Sea near Masalembo; 52 dead, 83 missing
detail: The Surabaya-Banjarmasin ferry Virgo Transport 8, carrying 243 people, capsized in 3-metre waves near the Masalembo islands; by 25 September BASARNAS divers had recovered 52 bodies, 108 were rescued and 83 remained missing.

title: Anak Krakatau lowered to Level II; new islets formed
detail: The Geological Agency lowered Anak Krakatau from Level III to Level II from Sep 21 after the Sep 4-6 eruptions, which it said formed two new islets and expanded the edifice by 32.8 ha; 2 km crater and 1 km islet exclusion zones apply.

title: Solok flash floods: 2 dead, 474 evacuated
detail: Flash floods in Arosuka, Solok, killed 2, injured 4 and forced 474 to evacuate, damaging 87 homes; a 14-day emergency took effect Sep 22. VP Gibran visited and urged debris clearance.
